title: ORbital Atherectomy for Lesion Preparation in Patients With Chronic Limb-threatening ischEmia
official: ORbital Atherectomy for Lesion Preparation in Patients With Chronic Limb-threatening ischEmia
summary: ORACLE is a Europe-wide study that will follow 250 people with critical limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI). It aims to see how well orbital atherectomy (OA) works in real-life practice. OA is a procedure that uses a tiny spinning tool to gently remove hard calcium from inside an artery, helping to open the vessel so other treatments-like balloons or stents-can work better. The study focuses on people who have heavily calcified arteries in the femoropopliteal or infrapopliteal areas of the leg.
